content:
We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id for the template that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the reaction: DIBAL-H reduction of ester/nitrile to aldehyde, breaking C-O bond, changing bond order from double to single, forming aliphatic hydroxyl.

We have available input: from previous step make_5_lvl2-apply_template-2 answer: a list of lists of SMILES (precursors). Those are possible precursors when applying some template to the molecule. The list:

[
 ["C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO"],
 ["C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C"],
 ["C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO"]
]

These are three possible precursors. The target molecule (the one we need to apply template to) is not directly given, but likely the product after reduction: an aldehyde with aliphatic hydroxyl? Actually DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, so product is aldehyde. The precursors are likely the ester forms (with protecting groups). The template likely is "Ester to aldehyde reduction" (functional group broken: ester, formed: aldehyde). The template ID we need to find.

We need to search template catalog with criteria: functional_groups_broken includes "ester", functional_groups_formed includes "aldehyde". Also bond order changed: C=O double to C-O single? Actually carbonyl bond order changes from 2 to 1 (C-O single) and C=O becomes C=O? Wait reduction of ester to aldehyde: the C=O remains double, but the C-O single bond to O of alkoxy is broken, forming C-H. So bond broken: C-O single bond (the alkoxy). Bond order changed: maybe C=O stays double, but new C-H formed. But we can search with broken functional group "ester" and formed "aldehyde". Let's use search_template_catalog_by_criteria.

We need the target molecule SMILES. Not given directly. Could be the aldehyde product. The precursors list are esters (with protecting groups). The product likely is something like "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)C[C@H]1C)CO"? Actually the product after reduction would have aldehyde at the position of the ester: C(=O)O becomes CHO. So product SMILES maybe similar but with C=O and H. Hard to guess.

Alternative: maybe we can directly search templates that match the given precursor SMILES? Actually we need template that when applied to the molecule (target) reproduces the reaction. The target is the aldehyde product. The precursors are esters. So the template is reduction of ester to aldehyde. We need mapped_rxn (reaction SMILES with atom mapping) and template_id.

We could search templates with criteria and then test each with check_smiles_reaction_template_matching on the product SMILES? But we don't have product SMILES.

Maybe the system expects we retrieve the template that was used to generate those precursors earlier. The previous step "make_5_lvl2-apply_template-2" likely applied a template to the molecule and got precursors. So the template ID used there is the one we need. We need to retrieve that ID. Perhaps the system stored it? Not given.

We could try to infer by searching for templates that produce those precursors from a product. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken = ["ester"], functional_groups_formed = ["aldehyde"], limit maybe 5. Then we can check each template's applicability to one of the precursor SMILES? Actually we need to check if template matches the product (aldehyde). But we don't have product.

Maybe we can use apply_template with each candidate template to the product? Not possible.

Alternative: maybe the template ID is known common: e.g., template for "Ester to aldehyde reduction (DIBAL-H)" might have ID 12345? Not sure.

We need to use tools to find template. Let's search with criteria.
